<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 193.1103. This likely corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion, giving a neutral monoisotopic mass of about 192.103 Da. The isotopic pattern (≈12 % M+1) suggests roughly ten carbon atoms (≈1.1 % × 10 ≈ 11 %). A formula that matches the neutral mass and the carbon count is C₁₀H₁₈O₂ (exact neutral mass = 170.13068 Da; [M+Na]⁺ = 193.1199 Da, within typical instrument tolerance). This formula also yields the observed M+1 intensity from the natural ¹³C abundance. Therefore the molecular formula of the molecule in the sample is C10H18O2.</thought>
<final_answer>C10H18O2</final_answer>
